newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's Di Tella hopes for U.S. non-NATO status.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Di Tella hopes for U.S. non-NATO status.

text.p: Argentine Foreign Minister Guido di Tella meets U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright in Washington on Friday hoping for clear signals on when Argentina may be awarded key U.S. ally status.

Albright said this week that Washington was likely to grant Argentina what she called "symbolic" status as a major non-NATO partner, putting it on the same footing as Israel, Egypt, Japan, South Korea and Jordan.
"This is public evidence of ... our good relations with the United States," Di Tella said on Thursday in Buenos Aires.

Di Tella, who promoted "carnal relations" with Washington early in the Carlos Menem administration, said he hoped the status would be confirmed before President Bill Clinton visits Argentina in October as part of a Latin American tour.

Menem has been eager for the designation in recognition for making Argentina a leading U.S. ally in South America, for its military support role in the 1991 Gulf War and its part in international peacekeeping from Croatia to Cyprus and Haiti.

The status would allow Argentina's armed forces -- which have had conscription scrapped and their budget slashed since the return to democracy in 1983 -- to buy on a priority basis excess items of ammunition and spare parts from the Pentagon.
Albright said other Latin American countries, including Chile, could be granted similar status.
But Argentine opposition parties warned that if Argentina gets such status before its neighbors, there could be tension.

"The possibility that Argentina will become a non-NATO military ally ... bolsters the position of the military and civilian sectors of Chile and Brazil, which do not want to deepen the current integration process," Deputy Juan Pablo Cafiero of Argentina's center-left Frepaso party said.
Argentina and Brazil have joined their smaller neighbors Paraguay and Uruguay in a new regional trade bloc called the Mercosur. Chile is an associate Mercosur partner.
